doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Getting record labels, then and now
summary: Labels came easily in his twenties; today artists often pay themselves. He mentions a Japan recording with Ray Brown.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What was it like to get record labels to record you? Has it been hard over the years?

Well it was easy for me, I guess I was in my 20s, 22, 24, 22, 23, 24, just like the young lions today only maybe a little different. So I think with the help of my friend or I don’t know how it came about but I got an offer to do the four albums for Bethlehem, but recently it’s been very hard, from my conversations with other people, either you have to, even the bigger names like one you told me, Roger Kellaway, you have either putting up the money yourself or I’m not sure, but it’s been harder recently to do it. I had one thing that I did with somebody, a home recording in a little place like this, I was in the other room and we did a thing where I was scat singing and they’ve been playing it out here a little bit, but the record isn’t out yet, the CD isn’t out yet. I could have brought that one but I didn’t bring it yet. You showed me a good copy on this thing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
Yeah. It sounds beautiful off of the LP you know?

Yeah, wow. There’s some student from Italy that came over here and he thought I was like Charlie Parker, “You’re a genius” blah-blah-blah. Anyhow he wanted to get a copy of this Catalyst thing. And I have so much clutter in my place that I couldn’t reach it, I don’t know where it is. It’s somewhere. But I have to send him a copy I think. The other thing is I did an album, I went to Japan with Ray Brown, Hank Jones and Alan Dawson. And we did a recording over there that is a CD. And he was supposed to send me a copy, because I don’t have a copy of the CD, it’s kind of hard to find but it’s out there somewhere. I don’t know why I mentioned that but just going around. Free association.
